svg.title: Proposition 21 - Physical-Descriptor Refinement and Residual Persistence
svg.desc: What this figure shows: Proved descriptor-refinement theorem for deterministic nested physical descriptors and finite stochastic variables.. Visible guideposts include: A residual is audited by adding physical detail, not interpreted in isolation.; NESTED PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION; Fine descriptors refine coarse descriptors; Ω → T_f → T_c; T_f = f(Ω), T_c = c(T_f); Every fine fiber lies inside one coarse fiber; refinement adds declared physical detail.. How to read it: follow the diagram in the direction of its arrows and use each box, panel, inequality, or highlighted region only with the meaning printed beside it. Main takeaway: this is the visual companion to Proposition 21; the proposition document supplies the assumptions, proof, and exact scope of every implication. Scientific status: Proposition 21 theorem/certificate visual. It is not independent empirical evidence and does not, by itself, identify a physical or latent variable with consciousness.
svg.text: P21 · Physical-Descriptor Refinement and Residual Persistence
A residual is audited by adding physical detail, not interpreted in isolation.
Every fine fiber lies inside one coarse fiber; refinement adds declared physical detail.
Unresolved target collisions can only disappear
A collision that survives the finer descriptor also existed at the coarse level.
A refinement may resolve a coarse collision, but cannot create a new one.
Residual decrease equals captured target information
Therefore R(T_f) ≤ R(T_c); valid physical refinement cannot raise the residual.
Residual persistence becomes a trajectory, not a single number
Each drop is exactly the target-relevant information supplied by the added physical detail.
A positive terminal residual challenges the finest declared descriptor; it does not establish nonphysical ontology or physical completeness.
